signatures.description: Implement a Petri-net analysis engine in Go reading JSON from stdin: {"places":[...],"transitions":[{"name":"t1","in":{"p1":2},"out":{"p2":3},"inhibit":["p3"]}],"initial":{...},"queries":[{"marking":{...}}]}, where inhibitor arcs block firing only on a strictly positive token count and transitions with empty in/out sets are self-looping sources. For every query emit "coverable", "uncoverable", or "unbounded" using a Karp-Miller tree with omega acceleration, and for unbounded queries also emit a concrete transition cycle witnessing unboundedness; plain omega comparison is known not to close the tree for all nets, so add Finkelstein generalized-coverability acceleration and prove termination by reporting the number of accelerated nodes. Additionally emit, per net, the shortest firing sequence (ties broken lexicographically by transition name) reaching a deadlock marking, or "no-deadlock" if none is reachable, using a marking hash that is canonical under place permutation.
